newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWF raises 1997/98 Australian wheat crop forecast.
newsitem.headline: AWF raises 1997/98 Australian wheat crop forecast.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) said on Tuesday it raised its preliminary forecast for the 1997/98 (April-March) wheat crop to 17.89 million tonnes from 17.81 million tonnes forecast last month.
But the forecast is still well down on 1996/97's record 22.34 million tonne wheat crop.
AWF put the wheat area estimate at 10.8 million hectares, against 10.9 million in 1996/97.
AWF said Australian wheat growers had been encouraged by the low levels of world wheat stocks and the recent strong rises in export wheat prices.

"The high quality of the 1996/97 Australian wheat harvest saw heavy deliveries to the export pool and low tonnages were retained on farms for post-harvest trading," AWF said in its second 1997/98 wheat forecast.
As a result, domestic wheat prices were trading above export parity and this was expected to continue until September.
"Given these strong market signals, growers have plans for another large wheat crop," AWF said.
Subsoil moisture in Queensland and northern New South Wales was excellent, but rain was needed with some urgency in these early maturing, high protein areas to enable planting.
Some rain over the weekend is expected to be topped up with further rain over the next few days in southern New South Wales.
This rain would be used for the preparation of land for the early crops, canola and lupins, AWF said.
Rain in Victoria over the weekend had been useful and important in consolidating sowing intentions but more was needed or else wheat intentions would start to slip.
Weekend rains was received on the South Australian west coast where growers are preparing ground for sowing.
